A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Uni-X research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite added related work, reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original Uni-X benchmark results, architectural and loss-masking ablations, gradient-conflict measurements and inference-throughput evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental outcomes, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations and supplementary gradient and throughput analyses.

M1.justification: The modality-specific end layers, shared middle layers, tokenization, modality routing, forward propagation and training objective remain unchanged. The instruction-loss masking procedure is also retained.

E1.justification: Training corpora and evaluated text, generation, understanding and editing tasks are unchanged. T2I-CompBench/MSCOCO, Code/Math/Wiki analyses and in-context examples already appear in v2; agent-related tasks in the new related-work appendix are only discussed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments, including Shared Transformer, MoT, HardMoE and UniFork in Table 4. Newly discussed methods such as OneCAT, VARGPT, Harmon and MetaQueries are not added to evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The 28B-token controlled comparisons, 140B/240B scaling settings, model sizes, hyperparameters, GenEval prompt rewriting and inference protocol are retained. The expanded reproducibility statement restates existing settings rather than reporting a changed evaluation design.

E4.justification: Loss-masking and layer-allocation ablations, domain and attention-module gradient analyses, generated-image examples and in-context cases are unchanged. The existing appendix analyses move to renumbered sections; none is newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same gradient averaging over more than 60 minibatches and 2M tokens, along with identical shaded gradient-conflict plots. No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty procedures or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported result entries, plotted outcomes and qualitative examples match throughout. Examples include GenEval 82/83 in Table 2, the Uni-X average of 41.6 in Table 4 and throughput of 910.2 tokens/s in Table 10; appendix results are likewise unchanged.

T1.justification: The gradient-conflict definitions, conditional-entropy expression, propagation and loss equations (1–6) are unchanged. The appendix argument comparing separated attention cost a²+b² with fully shared cost (a+b)² is also retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same gradient-conflict diagnosis, architectural contribution, efficiency/scalability claims and comparison with larger 7B models. No main scientific contribution is added or withdrawn.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.1 argues that unified models can reduce the context and computational overhead of multi-agent or multi-model pipelines for reasoning and tool calling. This extends the applicability discussion without agent experiments; existing result interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement newly describes repository contents including preprocessing utilities, configuration files and reproduction instructions. It replaces the anonymous repository pointer with the GitHub address already present in v2's abstract, refining access documentation without establishing a new code release.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.1 substantially expands literature coverage through OneCAT, VARGPT, Harmon and MetaQueries, then adds a broader positioning argument involving agents, search, recommendation and efficiency techniques. TokLIP is also newly cited in the introduction. This extends the research context beyond the earlier architecture-focused discussion.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and grammar edits, expands the reproducibility statement, adds acknowledgments and a related-work appendix, and updates affiliation/header text. The main narrative remains intact, while earlier appendix sections A.1–A.7 become A.2–A.8.

P2.justification: All eight figures and eleven tables are retained. Changes include resizing Figures 1 and 6, repositioning Table 5, adjusting table spacing and highlighting, simplifying Table 10's header, and adding conference headers with associated layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves context through coverage of additional unified architectures and clarifies repository contents and access guidance. These are useful documentation gains, while the method and empirical support remain unchanged. The broader agent-efficiency argument is untested, limiting the benefit of the expanded positioning.
